'''Charles Julien Brianchon''' (19 December 1783 &ndash; 29 April 1864) was a French [[mathematician]] and [[chemist]].

==Life==
He entered into the [[École Polytechnique]] in 1804 at the age of eighteen{{dubious|date=May 2013}}, and studied under [[Monge]], graduating first in his class in 1808, after which he took up a career as a [[lieutenant]] in [[Napoleon Bonaparte|Napoleon]]'s [[artillery]]. Later, in 1818, Brianchon became a [[professor]] in the Artillery School of the [[Royal Guard (France)|Royal Guard]] at [[Vincennes]].

==Work==
Brianchon is best known for his [[mathematical proof|proof]] of ''[[Brianchon's theorem]]'' (1810).

Brianchon's book ''Mémoire sur les lignes du second ordre'' (Paris, 1817) is available online [https://archive.org/download/mmoiresurlesli00bria/mmoiresurlesli00bria.pdf].
